title: 2024 HMMT November Team Problem 8
statement:
Compute the unique real number \(x<3\) such that

\[\sqrt{(3-x)(4-x)}+\sqrt{(4-x)(6-x)}+\sqrt{(6-x)(3-x)}=x\]

solutions.text:
The given equation implies

\[\begin{aligned}
& (\sqrt{3-x}+\sqrt{4-x}+\sqrt{6-x})^{2} \\
& =(3-x)+(4-x)+(6-x) \\
& \quad+2(\sqrt{(3-x)(4-x)}+\sqrt{(4-x)(6-x)}+\sqrt{(6-x)(3-x)}) \\
& =13-3 x+2 x=13-x
\end{aligned}\]

As \(\sqrt{3-x}+\sqrt{4-x}+\sqrt{6-x}\) is nonnegative,

\[\sqrt{3-x}+\sqrt{4-x}+\sqrt{6-x}=\sqrt{13-x}\]

We repeatedly rearrange, square both sides, and simplify:

\[\begin{aligned}
\sqrt{3-x}+\sqrt{4-x} & =\sqrt{13-x}-\sqrt{6-x} \\
7-2 x+2 \sqrt{(3-x)(4-x)} & =19-2 x-2 \sqrt{(13-x)(6-x)} \\
\sqrt{(3-x)(4-x)} & =6-\sqrt{(13-x)(6-x)} \\
(3-x)(4-x) & =36-12 \sqrt{(13-x)(6-x)}+(13-x)(6-x) \\
2 x-17 & =2 \sqrt{(13-x)(6-x)} \\
4 x^{2}-68 x+289 & =4(13-x)(6-x) \\
8 x & =23 \Longrightarrow x=\frac{23}{8} .
\end{aligned}\]
